address: Our Lady Of The Assumption R C Church and Assumption Priory, Victoria Park Square, London, E2 9PB
description: Observation requested by Diocese of Westminster Churches Committee for the existing boiler equipment is approximately 15 years old. Only 25% of the boilers are currently working, parts are obsolete and no longer available. The boilers provide heating for the Church and it is imperative that the building is heated sufficiently to protect the historic fabric. New smaller boilers, valves, pressurisation unit and finned tube heaters are required to redesign the system. It is expected that efficiency of the system will be 30-40% more efficient and will improve the comfort of the parishioners. It will lower heating costs and environmental impact in line with the Churches Net Zero targets. Limited works are required externally i.e. removing the existing flues in an interior courtyard and replacing with new black powder coated flues. There is limited loss of historic fabric of the Church as a result of the proposals.

address: Caxton Hall Community Centre & Adjoining Land, Caxton Grove, E3 2EE
description: Application for Non-Material amendment to planning permission ref: PA/24/00164, Dated 06/12/2024. Non Material amendment(s) Sought: This pack sets out a Non-Material Amendment to planning permission PA/24/00164 for Caxton Grove. The amendment arises from one technical decision: the consented communal air source heat pump (ASHP) heat network is replaced by individual exhaust air heat pumps (EAHPs) serving each of the 36 dwellings. Every other change in the drawing package follows from it. The case for the energy strategy itself is made in the Whitecode Energy Feasibility Strategy submitted with this application; this pack sets out what the change means for the drawings. The consented strategy provided a site-wide heat network, sized and located to future-proof a connection to a district heat network. Whitecode confirm that no connectable network exists ? both identified East London Energy networks lie over 500 m from the site and the operator has confirmed that connection is not viable ? so the safeguarding benefit cannot be realised, while the network's distribution and standing losses would be incurred from day one. On a like-for-like basis the amended scheme saves 76% of regulated carbon site-wide against 65% for the communal option. The architectural consequences are all reductions. The two rooftop ASHP enclosures (1.6 × 5.4 m each) and their louvred plant screens are removed from the roof and from the elevations; the basement ? which housed only the Energy Centre and the water tanks ? is omitted; and the ground floor gains active frontage where plant louvres are no longer required. Photovoltaic capacity is retained at 24.8 kWp and is now distributed across both roofs. There is no change to the number, mix or size of dwellings (36 units), to the number of storeys or the storey heights, to the building footprint or to the site layout and landscaping. The external palette follows the consented specification, with the brick types and the metalwork RAL now confirmed;

description: Minor Material Amendments to planning permission PA/15/00360 dated 18/12/2015, to amend the wording of condition 10 (Travel Plan) and condition 19 (School Hours). The amended conditions would read as follows: Condition 10 currently reads: Prior to the first occupation of the development a Travel Plan shall be submitted to and agreed in writing by the local planning authority. The Travel Plan shall include details relating to public transport, car and cycle parking demand and walking to the development for employees, school children and parents. The development shall be operated in accordance with the approved Travel Plan. Condition 10 as proposed: The development shall be operated in accordance with the approved Travel Plan ref. 111045-PEF-XX-XX-TRP-H-00003, dated July 2026. Reason: To encourage sustainable transport and to ensure the amenity of nearby residents is not compromised in accordance with Policies D.DH8, D.ES9, S.TR1, D.TR2 and D.TR3 of the Tower Hamlet Local Plan (2020). Condition 19 currently reads: The teaching hours of the school hereby permitted shall start no later than 8:30 and finish no earlier than 3.55. Condition 19 as proposed: The teaching hours of the school hereby permitted shall start no later than 8.15am and finish no later than 3.00pm. For clarity, 'teaching hours' are the minimum core hours that pupils are required to be in school and do not include after school clubs and activities. Reason: To stagger the teaching hours of the new school with those of St Luke's Primary School to avoid congestion on the public highway and ensure the amenity of nearby residents is not compromised, in accordance with Policies D.DH8, D.ES9, S.TR1, D.TR2 and D.TR3 of the Tower Hamlet Local Plan (2020).
